context_spans.label: section-lim-not-quasi-compact: the system (N, T_n) with basis singletons 1..n and I_n, X = discrete N as the inverse limit, and X not quasi-compact

standard_prerequisites: Context span 296-335: for each n the topology T_n on N with basis {1}, ..., {n}, I_n where I_n = naturals > n; each X_n = (N, T_n) is quasi-compact and the identity maps f_{n,m}: X_n -> X_m are continuous with the compatibilities f_{p,n} compose f_{n,m} = f_{p,m}, giving a directed inverse system of quasi-compact spaces

Context continues: X = (N, discrete) with f_n: X -> X_n continuous; the universal property check (any compatible system of maps g_n: (Y, S) -> (N, T_n) is a common set map g: Y -> N with all g^{-1}({n}) open in Y, hence continuous for S and T) shows X is the inverse limit; finally the infinite open covering of X by singleton sets has no inverse limit, so X is not quasi-compact
core_obligations: The context system ((X_n), (f_{n,m})) consists of quasi-compact topological spaces
By the context universal-property verification its limit is the discrete space X = (N, T)
X is not quasi-compact: the covering by singleton sets is an open covering of the discrete space with no finite subcover, as observed in the context
Hence the limit of the directed system is not quasi-compact
proof_roadmap: Instantiate the context system of quasi-compact spaces
Identify the limit as the discrete N via the context universal-property argument
Conclude with the singleton-cover observation from the context
